newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki rebounds clearly, but doubts remain.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki rebounds clearly, but doubts remain.

text.p: Shares staged a sharp rebound on Monday with Nokia and forestries heartened by U.S. stock gains to propel the HEX more than three percent ahead, but volume quite thin: brokers said investors remained hesitant.

The HEX general index rose 3.2 percent to 2,821.86 as advancers beat decliners 64 to 22 with 20 unchanged, and the FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark rose 3.14 percent to 982.20 points. Volume was a modest 435 milion with 52 percent in Nokia.
"This was a clear rebound," one broker said, but added that the trend did not yet look solid with a chance for prices to rise for another day or two, then consolidate.
"Investors were buying dollar-sensitive shares like UPM-Kymmene and Nokia," one broker said.
Telecoms major Nokia rose 20.00 markka to end at 301.00 and the forestry index surged over five percent amid talk of pulp price hikes.
Nokia was also helped by tech stock strength in the U.S. and by a new buy recommendation from Goldman Sachs during the session, brokers said.

Finland's largest forestry group UPM-Kymmene led other forestries higher, rising 6.00 markka to close at 111.00 in fair 35 million markka trade. Second largest Enso rose 2.50 to 44.50 in 19 million markka volume.
Plans for possible pulp price hikes from U.S., Swedish and Finnish producers helped put forestries back in focus, but brokers remained unsure they would emerge.
"These are only planned price increases, and they have been hard to implement," one broker said.
